Office · Standard

Alert Limit: 8 · Loot: Prize · For: a second or third session

The Objective

A memory stick in the desk drawer of the corner office. Empty after 6 p.m. except for a cleaning crew that comes through at 8.

What the Crew Sees at the Score

A small open-plan office with a corner room for the manager, two floors, entry from the ground-floor ventilation. In plain sight: a motion-sensor light system across the main floor, and a guard spider working the overnight shift. The second way in is the gap under the service door.

Present only what's visible. The intel, the threats, and the unknown obstacle are ST information — let Planning reveal the rest.

The office. A: the ground-floor vent. B: the gap under the service door, a squeeze. Red dashes: the two sensor beams. G: the guard spider and its loop. The stairs and the cable riser join the floors; the riser comes up inside the corner office. The manager's desk is 3 squares tall. Storyteller's copy: anything dashed in red is the unknown obstacle — keep it off what the crew sees.

One square = one spider. Gold letters are entry points, red tokens are where threats start, numbered circles are the Suggested Obstacles, and E1/E2 lie on the dashed gold escape route.

Intel the crew can uncover by Casing — one true detail per Success, and never more than this list (extra Successes buy nothing; Casing never reveals the unknown obstacle):

  • The two sensor beams each cover a known line of squares with a fixed timing gap.
  • The guard spider's patrol loops the perimeter every few rounds.
  • The drawer uses a standard lock.
  • The cable riser comes up behind the manager's desk.

It knows someone's inside, not where. Until it spots the crew (Chapter 16), it walks its loop of the upper floor from the stair landing: 28 squares, about 5 rounds at Speed 6, past the office door. Roll at the end of each lap (Chapter 14); on a 5–6, it takes the stairs down and walks the ground floor's east end.

Lap roll (1–2 the lap backwards, 3–4 rests a round, 5–6 the ground floor's east end): [[/gmr 1d6]]{Guard's lap}

ST information. Don't foreshadow it in the Score — let it arrive.

The cleaning crew came at 7 tonight, not 8. They're already here — upstairs, doing the corner office: a cleaner vacuuming inside with headphones on, the cart wedged in the doorway. They finish 6 rounds after the crew reaches the upper floor, then take the stairs down, park the cart across the vent, and prop the service door open for their bags.

Obstacles 1–4 are the heist: each takes two successful rolls (Partial or better). E1 and E2 are the suggested Escape obstacles: one successful roll each, and at least one of them never needs Athletics. Difficulties are for a calm location; the Alert raises them. Opposed means the creature rolls first, and its Successes + 1 are your Difficulty.

#ObstacleRoll (Difficulty)
1The motion sensors: two beams across the ground floor. Pattern known, timing tight.Cross in the gap: Stealth (3) · jam an emitter: Engineering (3), one beam per roll
2The guard spider. Professional, alert, doing the job — it is aware of the crew from the moment they're inside (+1 Alert each round it can see them). First real opposed roll.Stealth, opposed (its Perception 4) · fight: Brawl, opposed (its Brawl 3) — fights are loud · talk: Persuasion (4), not the Face · bribe: its Weakness (Chapter 16)
3(Unknown) The cleaners, in the corner office. The cart blocks the doorway; the vacuum is running.Past the cleaner: Stealth (1) · past the vacuum: Athletics or Tactics (2) · over the cart: Acrobatics (2)
4The locked desk drawer. Engineering moment.Engineering (3) · force it: Athletics (3), +1 Alert
E1Down with the stick — riser or stairs — and back through the beams.Stealth (3) · jam a beam for everyone: Engineering (3)
E2The cleaning cart is parked across the vent the crew planned to leave through. Out the propped service door instead, past the cleaners.Past the cleaners: Stealth (1) · time the vacuum: Tactics (2) · shove the cart: Athletics (3), +1 Alert
